answer: Tie sybil resistance to something identity cannot mint: slow accumulated stake. Each agent earns reputation through a voyage of completed, peer-attested tasks, and that record acts as an anchor — a clone created today has zero history and pays full bonds for months before anyone trusts it. I picture reputation like a comet's tail: visible, singular, and physically impossible to duplicate, since every attestation references one signing key. Rate-limit new accounts by age-weighted voting so a swarm of fresh sybils simply cannot reach quorum on any proposal.
